answer: The claimant plants a velvet survey flag at the exact nadir of a dune hollow at solar noon, when its shadow vanishes; the flag's dye lot is recorded against the dune register. Two dune wardens measure the flag's shadow at a named hour within three days and check the velvet grain against the register's sample. A flag off the nadir, a shadow too long, or a flag planted twice voids the season, burns a 230-credit stake, and bars the dune two seasons. One thousand fake flags mean one thousand nadir surveys made by hand plus one thousand velvet flags dyed one by one.
